basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 19-21.' and it opens 'VERS. 19-21.-- Et fuit terminus Chananaeorum venientibus a Sidone Geraram usque Gazam,'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 19-21.-- Et fuit terminus Chananaeorum venientibus a Sidone Geraram usque Gazam, donec egrediaris Sodomam, et Gomorrham, et Adamam, et Seboim, usque Lesam. Caeterae propria nomina retinent. Hoc tantum adnotandum videtur quod Lesa ipsa sit quae nunc Callirhoe dicitur, ubi aquae calidae prorumpentes in mare Mortuum defluunt.
